ITA-9.2.12 abhyaṅgaḥ अभ्यङ्गः
Application of oil to body
Procedure to induce oleation carried out by external application of an unctuous substance for therapeutic purposes and healthy well-being.

ITA-1.7.7 abhyanujñā अभ्यनुज्ञा
Unquestioning acceptance
Unconditional acceptance of different positions, including those which are inconclusive.

ITA-2.6.28 abhyavaharaṇa-śaktiḥ अभ्यवहरणशक्तिः
Ingestive power, food intake capacity
The capacity to ingest food, the amount of food which does not disturb an individual’s physiological functions. It differs from person to person and from time to time, being directly dependent on the individual’s digestive fire and psychological status.

ITA-1.9.4.4.11 The quality of being able to repeat an action or procedure to abhyāsaḥ acquire expertise, as exemplified by the saying “practice makes perfectः an important quality for physicians and pharmacists. अभ्यासः
Practice

ITA-5.13.4 ābhyantara-kṛmiḥ आभ्यन्तर-कृमिः
Internal worm infestation

ITA-9.2.5 ābhyantarasnehaḥ, snehapāna आभ्यन्तरस्नेहः, स्नेहपान
Internal oleation
The therapeutic administration of the appropriate dose of processed ghee, oil or any other unctuous substance internally to achieve oleation.

ābhyantarahetuḥ आभ्यन्तरहेतुः
Intrinsic cause
Internal factors such as dosha and affected structural components in the body which act as prime causes of disease manifestation when they deviate from the normal stage of equilibrium.
